FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.99  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.18  
DESCRIPTION: As written, `FindingEquivalenceClass` is a plain class with annotations and properties, but no `@dataclass` and no explicit `__init__`. `_compute_equivalence_classes()` instantiates it with keyword arguments, so the first non-empty call will raise `TypeError: FindingEquivalenceClass() takes no arguments`, making convergence detection fail at runtime.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `@dataclass` to `FindingEquivalenceClass` or implement an explicit constructor matching the call site.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.converged()` has no guard for the documented “not converged unless null_expected” empty-findings case. With empty findings for rounds `0..r`, `kappa_set(r)=1`, `kappa_rate(r)=1` for `r>=1`, `kappa_adopt(r)=1` by default, and `_veto(r)=False`, so the detector will report convergence as soon as `min_rounds_for_convergence` is reached.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit empty-corpus/null-expected policy to `converged()`, and fail closed when no findings exist unless the caller opts into a null-expected mode.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The severity veto is non-persistent. `_veto()` only checks novel classes in the current round, so a critical finding blocks convergence only on first appearance; if the same high-severity issue is repeated in later rounds, it is no longer novel and the veto disappears. This allows the system to declare convergence while a severe unresolved issue is still being reported.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Track unresolved severe classes across rounds and veto convergence until they are explicitly resolved, adopted, or cleared by a stronger policy than “not novel this round.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: `_tokenize_for_similarity()` removes semantically important words such as `not`, `no`, `before`, `after`, `only`, `under`, and `over` because they are in `_STOPWORDS`. That can turn opposite findings into the same token set, for example “input validated” and “input not validated”, causing false equivalence and overstated convergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove negators and other relation-bearing terms from the stopword list, or replace the generic stopword filter with one designed for technical defect descriptions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: Missing adoption data is treated as perfect adoption stability. `add_round_findings()` defaults `adoption_delta` to `0.0`, and `kappa_adopt()` converts that to `1.0`, so if the caller omits adoption data or collection fails, one of the three convergence brakes silently reports “fully stable.”  
PROPOSED_FIX: Represent missing adoption data as `None`, propagate that state explicitly, and either exclude the metric by policy or fail closed instead of mapping missing data to `1.0`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R4_CONV_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: [CROSS-COMPONENT — unverified from this scope] `_finding_similarity()` gives same-class findings a hard minimum similarity of `0.3` even with zero lexical overlap. Prior verified findings say the management layer can lower `tau_sim` to `0.3`; if that happens, every same-`flaw_class` pair becomes equivalent automatically, collapsing novelty and class counts.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Keep `tau_sim` strictly above the same-class floor, or remove the fixed `0.3` bonus so class match cannot by itself satisfy the equivalence threshold.  
VERIFIED: FALSE
